examples.en: I tied my hair with a rubber band.
The elastic has stretched out and my pants keep slipping down.
I tucked the papers under a rubber band.
The children are playing the rubber band jumping game.
If you pull the rubber band too hard, it snaps.
This rubber band got weak as I used it.

explain: 머리를 묶는 고무줄은 '머리끈'이라고도 해요. '고무줄놀이'는 고무줄을 높이 올리며 뛰어넘는 놀이 이름이에요. '고무줄 바지'는 허리가 늘어나는 바지예요.
explain_en: A rubber band for tying hair is also called a '머리끈'. '고무줄놀이' is the name of a game where you jump over a rubber band that keeps being raised. '고무줄 바지' means pants with a stretchy waist.

examples.en: The wall was stained, so I painted over it with white paint.
When the painting dries, I paint another layer on top.

examples.ko: 너무 여러 번 덧칠하면 색이 탁해져요.
examples.en: If you go over it too many times, the color gets muddy.
I want to put another coat of nail polish on.
I painted over the mistake to hide it.
Even without another coat, the color is pretty enough.

explain: 이미 칠한 곳 위에 또 칠할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '다시 칠하다'도 많이 말하고, 나쁜 것을 가리려고 꾸밀 때 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you paint over a spot that is already painted. In daily talk '다시 칠하다' is also common, and it can be used figuratively for covering up something bad.

examples.en: We ran out of toilet paper rolls.
I found an old scroll in the drawer.

examples.ko: 선생님이 두루마리에 큰 글씨로 이름을 쓰셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher wrote the name in big letters on the scroll.

examples.ko: 이 두루마리는 한 장씩 뜯어서 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tear this roll off one sheet at a time.
I rolled the painting into a scroll and brought it.
The roll rolled across the floor, so I quickly picked it up.

explain: 마트에서는 '두루마리 휴지'처럼 말아 놓은 휴지를 부를 때 앞에 붙여요. 한 장씩 뽑아 쓰는 휴지는 '각 티슈'라고 해요. 옛날에 길게 써서 둘둘 말아 둔 종이도 두루마리라고 불러요.
explain_en: For rolled-up tissue you put it in front, as in '두루마리 휴지'. Tissue you pull out one sheet at a time is called '각 티슈'. A long sheet of paper written on and rolled up in the old days is also called 두루마리.

examples.ko: 산에 오를 때 로프를 꼭 묶어요.
examples.en: When I climb a mountain, I always tie a rope.
I hold the rope firmly so it will not break.
I tied the boat to the port with a rope.
I hung one end of the rope on a tree.
I tied my body to the rope and climbed up slowly.
The firefighter packed a rope and equipment and headed out.

explain: 같은 물건을 '밧줄'이라고도 해요. 등산·암벽 등반·캠핑에서는 '로프', 배를 묶는 굵은 줄이나 일반 말에서는 '밧줄'이 더 자연스러워요. 가는 줄은 '끈'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The same thing is also called '밧줄'. In hiking, rock climbing, and camping people say '로프', while for the thick line that ties up a boat or in general talk '밧줄' sounds more natural. A thin line is a '끈'.

examples.ko: 병뚜껑이 너무 꼭 닫혀서 열 수가 없어요.
examples.en: The bottle cap is on so tight that I can't open it.
A bottle cap is lying on the table.
I drank the juice and closed the bottle cap again.

examples.ko: 아이가 병뚜껑을 입에 넣지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful that the child doesn't put the bottle cap in their mouth.
I collect bottle caps and throw them in the recycling bin.

examples.ko: 병뚜껑이 잘 안 열리면 수건으로 감싸고 돌려 보세요.
examples.en: If the bottle cap won't open, wrap it in a towel and twist it.

explain: '뚜껑'은 모든 뚜껑을 가리키고, '병뚜껑'은 병에 붙은 뚜껑만 가리켜요. '열다, 닫다'와 함께 쓰고, 음료병의 뚜껑을 열 때는 '따다'도 써요.
explain_en: '뚜껑' means any lid, while '병뚜껑' is specifically the cap of a bottle. It goes with '열다' and '닫다', and for opening a drink bottle '따다' is also used.

examples.en: The file was copied to another folder.

examples.ko: 사진이 잘못 복사돼서 두 장이 됐어요.
examples.en: The photo got copied by mistake and became two.
The content must not be copied as it is.
The email address won't copy.
Please leave the copied documents here.

examples.ko: 그 글이 인터넷에서 계속 복사되고 있어요.
examples.en: That post keeps getting copied around the internet.

explain: 복사되다는 파일이나 서류처럼 복사되는 물건이 주어일 때 써요. 복사하는 사람이 주어이면 '복사하다'를 써요. '복사돼요', '복사됐어요'처럼 '되어'가 '돼'로 줄어드는 것도 기억하세요.
explain_en: 복사되다 is used when the thing being copied, like a file or a document, is the subject. When a person does the copying, use 복사하다. Remember that 되어 shortens to 돼, as in 복사돼요 and 복사됐어요.

examples.en: I like that the camera shutter sound is quiet.
The store shutter was halfway down.

examples.ko: 상점들은 밤 열 시에 셔터를 내려요.
examples.en: The shops pull their shutters down at ten at night.

examples.ko: 셔터는 한 번만 눌러도 사진이 찍혀요.
examples.en: Even one press of the shutter takes a photo.
The shutter was covered in graffiti, so I cleaned it.
I locked both the shutter and the door and left work.

explain: 카메라와 가게, 두 곳에서 모두 써요. 카메라는 '셔터를 누르다', 가게는 '셔터를 올리다', '셔터를 내리다'로 동사가 달라져요.
explain_en: It is used for both cameras and stores. With a camera you press it, while with a store you raise or lower it, so the verb changes.

examples.en: I measured the room temperature with a thermometer.
The numbers look odd, maybe the thermometer is broken.
The thermometer is in the drawer.
I hung the thermometer outside the window.

examples.ko: 창문 옆 온도계에 영하라고 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The thermometer by the window says below zero.
The thermometer reading went over thirty degrees.

explain: 몸의 열을 잴 때는 '체온계', 방이나 날씨 온도를 잴 때는 '온도계'를 써요. 도구를 쓸 때는 '온도를 재다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: To measure body heat you use a '체온계', and to measure a room or the weather you use a '온도계'. When using the tool, you say '온도를 재다'.

examples.en: I put a small decoration on the living room shelf.

examples.ko: 이 장식품은 여행 가서 산 거예요.
examples.en: I bought this decoration while traveling.
I took out the box of Christmas decorations.
The decoration fell and broke.

examples.ko: 값비싼 장식품보다 직접 만든 게 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer something handmade over an expensive decoration.
I bought a flowerpot at the store to use as decoration.

explain: '장식품'은 쓸모보다 꾸미는 용도로 놓는 물건에 써요. 몸에 하는 것은 '액세서리'라고 해요. 같이 쓰는 동사는 '놓다', '달다', '걸다'예요.
explain_en: '장식품' is for things placed mainly to decorate rather than to be useful. Things you wear are called '액세서리'. It goes with the verbs '놓다', '달다' and '걸다'.

examples.en: The waiter brought water glasses on a tray.
I carefully lifted the tray with both hands.
The tray is so heavy that my arms hurt.
I arranged the fruit nicely on the tray.
Leave the tray to dry after washing it.
I am looking for a flat plate like a tray.

explain: '쟁반을 들다', '쟁반에 담다/올리다'처럼 써요. 음식을 담는 그릇은 '접시'이고, 쟁반은 컵이나 그릇을 올려서 나르는 판이라 달라요. 식당에서 직접 음식을 가져갈 때도 쟁반을 써요.
explain_en: It is used like '쟁반을 들다' and '쟁반에 담다' or '올리다'. A '접시' is a dish that holds food, while a '쟁반' is a board that carries cups and dishes, so they are different. You also use a tray when you carry your own food at a restaurant.

en: electric kettle (in Korean usage); coffee pot

examples.en: I boil water in the kettle and drink tea.
The kettle broke, so I bought a new one.
The kettle in the office is always on.
I boiled water for ramen in the kettle.
You have to wipe the inside of the kettle clean.

examples.ko: 커피포트를 쓴 뒤에는 전원을 꼭 뽑으세요.
examples.en: After using the kettle, be sure to unplug it.

explain: 한국에서 '커피포트'는 물을 끓이는 전기 주전자를 가리킬 때가 많아서, 커피를 내리는 기계로 알면 헷갈려요. 커피를 내리는 기계는 '커피 머신'이나 '커피메이커'라고 해요.
explain_en: In Korea '커피포트' often means an electric kettle for boiling water, so thinking of it as a coffee-brewing machine can be confusing. A machine that brews coffee is called a '커피 머신' or '커피메이커'.

examples.en: I pressed the bicycle pedals as hard as I could.

examples.ko: 페달이 고장 나서 자전거가 안 가요.
examples.en: The pedal is broken, so the bike will not go.

examples.ko: 피아노 페달은 소리를 오래 이어 줘요.
examples.en: The piano pedal makes the sound last longer.
The child stepped onto the pedal with a small foot.

examples.ko: 페달 없는 전동 자전거를 타 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried an electric bike with no pedals.
I adjusted both the pedals and the seat to fit the child.

explain: '페달을 밟다'처럼 '밟다'와 함께 써요. 자전거, 자동차의 '액셀 페달', '브레이크 페달', 피아노에서 발로 밟는 장치를 페달이라고 불러요.
explain_en: It goes with 밟다, as in 페달을 밟다. Foot-operated parts are called 페달, such as bike pedals, car 액셀 페달 and 브레이크 페달, and piano pedals.
